Article: Sixty Is Not a Waiting Room: The Art of Living Fully

Why let worry and sadness overshadow later life when experience is our greatest asset? Reflections on letting go of the past, easing stress and cultivating joy.

Read the full article

Full approved article

I often receive private messages from friends and followers in their fifties and sixties. Many describe the same troubling feeling: a heaviness of heart, fading enthusiasm, and sadness creeping into their days—as though life's train had already reached its final station.

We must be candid with ourselves: the length of our lives rests in the hands of Almighty God. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reminded us that the lifespans of his community are generally between sixty and seventy years. Knowing that the road ahead may be shorter should inspire us to live more fully and purposefully, not cause us to withdraw and let our spirits fade.

Experience Is Your Capital

By sixty, you have passed through life's great milestones. You have lost loved ones, faced challenges, and learned lessons that money cannot buy. It makes little sense to gather such a wealth of wisdom and maturity, only to squander it on apprehension, regret, or revisiting old sorrows.

Every minute at this stage of life is a genuine treasure. You can invest it in peace of mind and good deeds, or allow it to slip away through anxiety about the past and fear of what is yet to come.

Making Peace with the Past

To truly enjoy the years ahead, begin by putting down the burdens you have carried. A heart weighed down by grudges and disputes cannot fully taste happiness. This stage of life calls for a particular kind of spiritual courage:

Cultivating Joy and Protecting Energy

Looking after your mental wellbeing at this stage is a conscious choice, not a matter of chance. Neither body nor mind can comfortably withstand the constant strain of chronic stress and persistently elevated cortisol, which can take a toll on health and mood.

Happiness begins with a decision you make within yourself. Nobody is going to knock on your door carrying four kilograms of ready-made joy! Yet there will always be people who bring their worries, negative energy, and discouraging conversations into your company. This is when you must protect your emotional space with firm but thoughtful boundaries. Step away from those who spread gloom, and set limits with anyone who drains your spirit—even someone close to you. Affection and goodwill need not be lost; and, God willing, our finest reunion will be in Paradise. Here on earth, however, your peace of mind deserves care and priority.

Conclusion: Leave a Positive Legacy

Live each day of your sixties as a gift in its own right. Put your experience to good use, cleanse your heart, guard your peace against needless negativity, and approach this chapter with the spirit of an adventurer who has finally grasped the true value of time.
